notes: Cover panel re-shoot of zar-08-kesar-ink: standing, full length, headroom for the tall crop.
prompt: Editorial fashion photograph for an Indian handloom label's festive lookbook. Tall vertical 9:16 frame.
GARMENT (a real product; match the reference photos exactly, including colours, borders and motifs):
- Saree: the vivid magenta-purple mul cotton saree from the first three references, with an emerald-green border carrying fine gold zari lines. Plain purple body, matte, very light.
- Blouse: the sleeveless emerald-green blouse with a scoop neckline from the last two references.
- The pallu lifts in the wind behind her shoulder like a sail, showing its green-and-gold border against the sky.
MUSE: a slender woman in her early twenties with a pixie crop, small gold studs and a nose pin, a single thick gold kada. Eyes closed, face tilted to the breeze, serene smile.
MOMENT AND PLACE: Golden hour on an old Kolkata rooftop: she stands with the wind lifting her pallu behind her, kites dotting the sky, rows of clay diyas on the parapet.
LIGHT: Low golden sun behind and to the side, the magenta saree glowing translucent where the pallu lifts.
COVER FRAMING (this photograph becomes one tall, narrow panel of the lookbook's opening page, behind a large title):
- POSE: she is standing upright, full length, head to toe in frame; ignore any seated or kneeling pose mentioned above.
- HEADROOM: the top quarter of the frame is calm, empty background (sky, wall, foliage or soft darkness); her head sits about a quarter of the way down, never near the top edge.
- Subject centred horizontally and filling the middle third of the width, so a narrow vertical crop keeps all of her.
- Keep the background simple and softly out of focus; nothing busy behind her face.
- CAMERA: eye level, 50mm lens at f/2.8, gentle depth of field, medium-format look with fine grain.
